record.title: Durocher–Gunderson–Li–Skala conjecture on cycles in triangle-free graphs
record.statement:
Let $n\geq 4$. A **triangle-free graph** is a graph containing no triangle, and $K_{a,b}$ denotes the complete bipartite graph with parts of sizes $a$ and $b$. **Durocher–Gunderson–Li–Skala conjecture.** For each $n\geq 4$, the balanced complete bipartite graph

$$
K_{\lceil n/2\rceil, \lfloor n/2 \rfloor}
$$

contains more cycles than any other $n$-vertex triangle-free graph. This conjecture asks for the extremal triangle-free graph maximizing the total number of cycles and arose from questions connected with path-finding algorithms. Its status is not resolved in the supplied source.
record.source_name: Andrii Arman, David S. Gunderson and Sergei Tsaturian, “Triangle-free graphs with the maximum number of cycles”, arXiv:1501.01088 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1501.01088

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2015).

record.title: The assembly-generation conjecture below virtual cohomological dimension
record.statement: Let $\Gamma_{n,s}$ denote the relevant graph automorphism group, and let $A_\phi$ be the assembly map associated to a gluing $\phi$ producing the graph $X_{n,s}$. Write $2n+s-3$ for the virtual cohomological dimension of $\Gamma_{n,s}$. **Assembly-generation conjecture.** If $k\not=2n+s-3$, then $H_k(\Gamma_{n,s})$ is generated by the images of the assembly maps $A_\phi$ over all possible gluings producing $X_{n,s}$. The examples in the paper verify this for $n=1$ and $n=2$; the conjecture concerns generation in every homological degree except the virtual cohomological dimension.
record.source_name: James Conant, Allen Hatcher, Martin Kassabov and Karen Vogtmann, “Assembling homology classes in automorphism groups of free groups”, arXiv:1501.02351 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1501.02351

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2015).

record.title: The adjacency dimension bound for the join of a graph with a universal vertex
record.statement:
Let $H$ be a graph of order $n\ge 2$, let $K_1+H$ denote the graph obtained by adding a universal vertex to $H$, and let $\mathcal{C}(K_1+H)$ be its adjacency threshold. For $k\in\{1,\ldots,\mathcal{C}(K_1+H)\}$, write $\operatorname{adim}_k(G)$ for the $k$-adjacency dimension of a graph $G$. **Adjacency dimension bound.**

$$
\operatorname{adim}_k(K_1+H)\le\operatorname{adim}_k(H)+k.
$$

The bound gives an upper estimate for the adjacency dimension of a graph formed by adjoining a universal vertex, and the surrounding example shows that it can be tight. The supplied text does not state whether the bound has been proved or remains open.
record.source_name: A. Estrada-Moreno, Y. Ramirez-Cruz and J. A. Rodriguez-Velazquez, “On the adjacency dimension of graphs”, arXiv:1501.04647 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1501.04647

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2015).

record.title: The 3-extendability conjecture for bow-tie graphs
record.statement: Let $C_m$ be a cycle of even length $m\ge6$, let $P_n$ be a path of odd order $n\ge5$, and let $C_m\bowtie P_n$ denote their bow-tie graph. **3-extendability conjecture.** For any even integer $m\ge6$ and any odd integer $n\ge5$, the graph $C_m\bowtie P_n$ is $3$-extendable. This would provide an infinite family of $3$-extendable graphs with the stated bow-tie construction, extending the proved case involving $C_6\bowtie P_n$; the conjecture remains open in the source.
record.source_name: Hongliang Lu and David G. L. Wang, “Surface embedding of non-bipartite k-extendable graphs”, arXiv:1501.05398 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1501.05398

record.title: Zhang et al.'s Ramsey-number conjecture for odd cycles and even wheels
record.statement:
Let $C_n$ be the cycle on $n$ vertices and let $W_m:=C_m\ast K_1$ be the wheel on $m+1$ vertices. For integers $n<m$, with $n$ odd and $m$ even, the Ramsey number $r(C_n,W_m)$ is the least integer $N$ such that every red-blue coloring of the edges of $K_N$ contains either a red copy of $C_n$ or a blue copy of $W_m$.

**Zhang et al.'s conjecture.** For integers $n<m$, with $n$ odd and $m$ even,

$$
r(C_n,W_m)=2m+1.
$$

The conjecture concerns the remaining case of asymmetric Ramsey numbers for cycles and wheels identified in the paper: odd $n$ and even $m$ with $n<m<3(n-1)/2$.
record.source_name: Nicolás Sanhueza, “Stability and Ramsey numbers for cycles and wheels”, arXiv:1501.07786 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1501.07786

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2015).

record.title: Half-order immersion conjecture for graphs with independence number at most two
record.statement: Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, and let $\alpha(G)$ denote its independence number. An **immersion** of a graph $H$ in $G$ is a subgraph obtainable from $G$ by lifting edges and deleting vertices and/or edges. **Half-order immersion conjecture.** Any graph $G$ with $\alpha(G) \leq 2$ contains an immersion of $K_{\lceil n/2 \rceil}$. Since every color class has at most two vertices in such a graph, this conjecture is the natural half-order consequence of Abu-Khzam–Langston's restricted conjecture. The source proves that this statement is equivalent, for this graph class, to the restricted Abu-Khzam–Langston conjecture, but leaves both statements unresolved in general.
record.source_name: Sylvia Vergara, “Complete graph immersions in dense graphs”, arXiv:1502.01786 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1502.01786

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2015). “It remains open for $t \in \{5,6\}$. In 1943 Hadwiger suggested that the containment had to be the minor order, i.e. he conjectured that every $t$-chromatic graph contains $K_t$ as a minor.”

record.title: Mubayi–Verstraëte conjecture for odd-uniform hypergraphs without 2-regular subgraphs
record.statement:
Let $k$ be an integer with $2\nmid k$, and let $H$ be an $n$-vertex $k$-uniform hypergraph. A **full $k$-star** is the family of all $k$-edges containing a fixed vertex, and a matching is maximal when no additional edge can be added while preserving pairwise disjointness. **Mubayi–Verstraëte conjecture.** There exists an integer $n_k$ such that, for $n\geq n_k$, if $H$ has no $2$-regular subgraphs, then

$$
|H|\leq {{n-1}\choose{k-1}}+\left\lfloor\frac{n-1}{k}\right\rfloor.
$$

Equality holds if and only if $H$ is a full $k$-star together with a maximal matching disjoint from the full $k$-star. This addresses the extremal case when $k$ is odd and $2$ does not divide $k$; the source gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Jaehoon Kim, “Regular subgraphs of uniform hypergraphs”, arXiv:1502.02177 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1502.02177

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2015).

record.title: Cycle conjecture for exact skew-symmetric permutations
record.statement:
Let $\mathfrak{p}=(\tilde{s},\pi)$ be exact and skew-symmetric on $[n]^*\cup[n]^{-}$, with $D_{\mathfrak{p}}=p_r^{-1}$, and suppose that

$$
\pi(s_{i-1})=s_{2n+1-i},\qquad 1\leq i\leq n.
$$

**Cycle conjecture.** The elements $n$ and $s_n$ are in the same cycle of $\pi$.

This conjecture is introduced to provide a $2$-reversal in the critical case arising in the analysis of sorting signed permutations. The paper presents examples supporting it, but does not establish the claim; a broader version is stated later without the exactness assumption.
record.source_name: Ricky X. F. Chen and Christian M. Reidys, “A simple framework on sorting permutations”, arXiv:1502.07971 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1502.07971

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2015).

record.title: Monotonicity conjecture for computing the Laplacian p-spectral radius
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and for $p\geq 1$ let $mu^{(p)}(G)$ denote its Laplacian $p$-spectral radius. Consider the computational problem of finding $mu^{(p)}(G)$ from the input graph $G$. **Computational monotonicity conjecture.** If $q>p\geq 1$, then finding $mu^{(p)}(G)$ can be reduced to finding $mu^{(q)}(G)$ in polynomial time.

The conjecture is motivated by the fact that the cases $p=1$ and $p=\infty$ have different computational behavior: the former is computable in linear time, whereas the latter is NP-complete. It proposes that increasing $p$ does not make the corresponding exact-value problem computationally easier.
record.source_name: Elizandro Max Borba, Sebastian Richter, Eliseu Fritscher and Carlos Hoppen, “The p-spectral radius of the Laplacian”, arXiv:1612.02643 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.02643

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2016).

record.title: Burns–Macedonska generalized Andrews–Curtis conjecture
record.statement: Let $G$ be a finitely generated group of rank $n$. An ordered $n$-tuple is **normally generating** when its components normally generate $G$, and its recalcitrance is the least number of M-transformations needed to reach a generating $n$-tuple, with value infinity when no such transition exists. **Burns–Macedonska generalized Andrews–Curtis conjecture.** Every normally generating $n$-tuple of $G$ has finite recalcitrance. This generalizes the recalcitrance formulation of the classical Andrews–Curtis conjecture from finitely generated free groups to finitely generated groups; the source presents it as a generalized conjecture associated with Burns and Macedonska.
record.source_name: Luc Guyot, “On Andrews-Curtis conjectures for soluble groups”, arXiv:1612.06912 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.06912

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2016). “The Andrews-Curtis conjecture ($\AC$ conjecture) is a long-standing open problem in combinatorial group theory with a tight link to open problems in low-dimensional topology .”

record.title: Hamada's conjecture on p-ranks of geometric designs
record.statement: Let $D$ be a design with the parameters of a geometric design $G$ in $\operatorname{PG}(n,q)$ or $\operatorname{AG}(n,q)$, where $q=p^m$. Let the $p$-rank denote the rank of the incidence matrix over $\mathbb{F}_p$. **Hamada's conjecture.** The $p$-rank of $D$ is at least the $p$-rank of $G$, with equality if and only if $D$ is isomorphic to $G$. This is a generalization of the preceding projective-plane rank conjecture to designs with parameters arising from finite projective or affine geometries; no resolution is supplied in the source.
record.source_name: S. B. Balaji and P. Vijay Kumar, “Erasure Codes for Distributed Storage: Tight Bounds and Matching Constructions”, arXiv:1806.04474 (2018).
record.references:

record.title: Queen inside-out-polytope denominator conjecture
record.statement:
Let $F_q$ be the $q$th Fibonacci number and let $[F_q]=\{1,2,\ldots,F_q\}$. For the inside-out polytope associated with $q$ queens, let $D$ denote its denominator. **Queen denominator conjecture.** The denominator of the inside-out polytope for $q$ queens is exactly

$$
\operatorname{lcm}[F_q],
$$

where $[F_q]=\{1,2,\ldots,F_q\}$. This is presented as a weaker denominator analogue of Kotěšovec's period conjecture and is left as an aim for the paper's theory.
record.source_name: Seth Chaiken, Christopher R. H. Hanusa and Thomas Zaslavsky, “A q-Queens Problem. IV. Attacking Configurations and Their Denominators”, arXiv:1807.04741 (2018).
record.references:

record.title: Fractional matching gap conjecture for critical graphs without 1-factors
record.statement:
Let $k\geq 3$ and let $G$ be a $k$-critical graph. Let $\mu(G)$ denote the matching number and $\mu_f(G)$ the fractional matching number. **Fractional matching gap conjecture.** If $G$ does not have a 1-factor, then

$$
\mu_f(G)>\mu(G).
$$

The source says this conjecture is unsolved even for critical graphs with a near-perfect matching, and that it would follow from the preceding fractional perfect matching conjecture.
record.source_name: Antje Klopp and Eckhard Steffen, “Fractional matchings, component-factors and edge-chromatic critical graphs”, arXiv:1903.12385 (2021).
record.references:

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.12385

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2019).

record.title: Stahl's multichromatic-number conjecture for Kneser graphs
record.statement:
Let $K(m,n)$ be the Kneser graph whose vertices are the $n$-subsets of $\{1,\ldots,m\}$, with two vertices adjacent when the corresponding subsets are disjoint. For an integer $r$, let $\chi_r(H)$ be the least integer $s$ such that $H$ admits a homomorphism to $K(s,r)$. **Stahl's conjecture.** If $k=an+b$, where $a\geq 1$ and $0\leq b\leq n-1$, then for $m\geq 2n$,

$$
\chi_k(K(m,n))=\chi_{an}(K(m,n))+\chi_b(K(m,n))=(a+1)m-2(n-b).
$$

This conjecture concerns the exact multichromatic numbers of Kneser graphs and is used in the paper to derive stronger lower bounds for chromatic numbers of exponential graphs. Its resolution is not specified in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Claude Tardif and Xuding Zhu, “A note on Hedetniemi's conjecture, Stahl's conjecture and the Poljak-Rödl function”, arXiv:1906.03748 (2019).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2016–2019). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1607.08780](https://arxiv.org/abs/1607.08780).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.03748

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of June 2019). “However, Shitov refuted this conjecture recently .”

record.title: Gamma-positivity conjecture for peak-refined inverse descent polynomials
record.statement:
For $n\geq1$ and $0\leq k\leq\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor$, define

$$
\hat{A}_{n,k}(t)=\sum_{\substack{\pi\in\mathfrak{S}_n\\\\ \operatorname{pk}(\pi)=k}}t^{\operatorname{ides}(\pi)+1}.
$$

A symmetric polynomial with center of symmetry $(n+1)/2$ is **$\gamma$-positive** when its expansion in the corresponding gamma basis has nonnegative coefficients. **Gamma-positivity conjecture.** The polynomials $\hat{A}_{n,k}(t)$ are $\gamma$-positive with center of symmetry $(n+1)/2$. This refines unimodality of the inverse-descent distribution among permutations with a fixed number of peaks.
record.source_name: Ira M. Gessel and Yan Zhuang, “Two-sided permutation statistics via symmetric functions”, arXiv:2306.15785 (2024).
record.references:

record.title: Convex-hull-size conjecture for optimal star-forest decompositions
record.statement:
Let $n\ge3$ be odd, and let $G$ be a complete geometric graph on $n$ vertices that can be decomposed into $\left\lceil\frac{n}{2}\right\rceil+1$ plane star-forests. **Convex-hull-size conjecture.** The convex hull of the vertex set $V(G)$ has size at most

$$
\left\lceil\frac{n}{2}\right\rceil+1.
$$

For even order, the source proves the analogous bound when $n=2k$, while the odd-order case is proposed as a conjecture. Its general validity remains open.
record.source_name: Todor Antić, Jelena Glišić and Milan Milivojčević, “Star-Forest Decompositions of Complete Graphs”, arXiv:2402.11044 (2024).

record.title: Wanless's conjecture on transversals in latin hypercubes
record.statement:
A **latin hypercube** of order $n$ and dimension $d$ is a $d$-dimensional array filled with $n$ symbols so that every line contains all symbols exactly once. A **transversal** is a diagonal containing all $n$ symbols. **Wanless's conjecture.** Every latin hypercube of odd order or odd dimension has a transversal.

The conjecture is trivial for order $2$ and easy to prove for order $3$. For order $4$, all latin hypercubes have transversals except the hypercube described as $\mathcal{Q}_4^d$ when $d$ is even; all latin hypercubes of order $5$ have transversals. The conjecture is also stated to have been extended from multidimensional permutations to all polystochastic matrices.
record.source_name: A. L. Perezhogin, V. N. Potapov, A. A. Taranenko and S. Yu. Vladimirov, “Characterization of polystochastic matrices of order 4 with zero permanent”, arXiv:2410.09546 (2024).
record.references:
**4 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2016–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1801.10306](https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.10306), [arXiv:1709.03071](https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.03071), [arXiv:1612.01797](https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.01797).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.09546

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2024). “Despite Montgomery's recent breakthrough , proving that every latin square of large order $n$ has a near transversal (a partial transversal of length $n-1$), the Ryser's conjecture is still open.”

record.title: Global rigidity conjecture for complete graphs in the infinity norm
record.statement: Let $d\geq 1$ and let $K_{2d+1}$ be the complete graph on $2d+1$ vertices. A realisation of $K_{2d+1}$ in $\ell_\infty^d$ assigns a point of $\mathbb{R}^d$ to each vertex, and it is **generic** when its coordinates satisfy no nontrivial algebraic relations over the rationals. The realisation is **globally rigid** if every realisation in $\ell_\infty^d$ with the same edge lengths is congruent to it. **Global rigidity conjecture.** The complete graph $K_{2d+1}$ has a generic globally rigid realisation in $\ell_\infty^d$. This is known in dimension $d=2$, while the assertion is unclear in the remaining dimensions.
record.source_name: Sean Dewar, “Uniquely realisable graphs in polyhedral normed spaces”, arXiv:2504.02139 (2025).
record.references:

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.02139

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2025).

record.title: Addario-Berry et al.'s antidirected-tree conjecture
record.statement: An **oriented graph** $G$ on $n$ vertices has an edge for each oriented edge of its underlying graph. An **antidirected tree** is an orientation of a tree in which every vertex has either in-degree $0$ or out-degree $0$, and the number of edges is its size. **Addario-Berry et al.'s conjecture.** For any integer $k\geq 1$, every oriented graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with more than $(k-1)n$ edges contains each antidirected tree with $k$ edges.
record.source_name: Andrzej Grzesik and Marek Skrzypczyk, “Antidirected paths in oriented graphs”, arXiv:2506.11866 (2025).
record.references:
**5 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2016–2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2411.13483](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.13483), [arXiv:2212.09876](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.09876), [arXiv:1912.04004](https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.04004), [arXiv:1610.00876](https://arxiv.org/abs/1610.00876).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.11866

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2025). “Since the antipath is the most natural orientation for which Conjecture is open, and known extremal examples witness that not containing an antipath seems to be the most restrictive condition, attention was recently drawn to the antipaths.”

record.title: Agrawal's conjecture on extremal triple arrays
record.statement:
Let $r$, $c$, and $d706_{cc}$ be parameters of a symmetric $2$-design on $r+c$ points, and suppose that $r-d706_{cc}>2$.

**Agrawal's conjecture.** If there is a symmetric $2$-$(r+c,r,d706_{cc})$ design with $r-d706_{cc}>2$, then there is an $(r\times c,r+c-1)$-triple array.

This conjecture asks whether Agrawal's construction from a symmetric design can always be completed from an unordered triple array to an ordered one under the stated condition. It remains open.
record.source_name: Alexey Gordeev and Lars-Daniel Öhman, “Resolvable Triple Arrays”, arXiv:2512.08681 (2026).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2016–2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1609.00152](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.00152).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.08681

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2025). “The following conjecture, which still remains open, was therefore implicit in Agrawal's work.”
